transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been making careless mistakes at work. Sales reports mostly—copying the wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or missing a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. Even when I thought I went over it. It’s been… frustrating.
How have you been feeling emotionally about these mistakes at work?
I don’t know… not great, I guess. Mostly embarrassed. I get irritated with myself, but I try not to make a big thing out of it.
Have you been having trouble paying attention to details outside of work as well?

Mostly I notice it at work. The sales reports, copying the wrong numbers off the dashboard, or missing a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. I’ll think I looked it over, but then something’s still wrong. Outside work… I don’t know, I haven’t really paid as much attention to that.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed about these mistakes at work?
Not really depressed, I don’t think. Anxious… maybe a little when it happens, but mostly I just feel embarrassed and annoyed with myself.
Have you been having any trouble remembering things that you normally would recall easily?
Yeah… some. It’s usually regular stuff I should remember, like returning calls, or paying a bill before I get a late notice. Sometimes I’ll tell my kids I’ll pick something up and then just… forget.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Yeah… especially if I’m stuck sitting for a while, like in a long meeting. I get this kind of buzzing feeling inside, and I’ll keep shifting around or tapping my foot. Sometimes I’ll find a reason to get up.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things that are not necessarily related to your work mistakes?
Not really… I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying all the time or anything.
Do you find yourself making careless mistakes or forgetting things in your personal life as well, not just at work?

Yeah… it happens at home too. I’ll forget to return calls, like from my attorney, or I’ll miss paying a bill until the late notice shows up. And sometimes I tell my kids I’ll pick something up for them and then I just don’t remember.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get tired like anyone, but nothing that really stands out lately.
Do you often feel the need to be active and have trouble engaging in quiet leisure activities?

Yeah… I guess so. Like if I’m watching a movie with my kids, I’ll end up checking my phone or getting up for no real reason. Same thing at church sometimes—I’ll whisper comments or shift around instead of just sitting quietly.
Have you been feeling guilty about things beyond just your work mistakes?
Not really… I mean, I feel bad when I mess something up, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling guilty about other things in general.
Do you often find yourself talking more than others in social situations?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’m always the one talking the most, but… maybe sometimes. I haven’t really paid close attention to it.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?
Yeah… I do that sometimes. Mostly in meetings. I’ll think I know what someone’s about to say and jump in, and then it turns out I cut them off or answered the wrong thing.
Do you often find yourself dominating conversations with friends or family, not just in work meetings?
I don’t think so… not that I’ve noticed. With friends or family I’m usually not trying to take over the conversation. Maybe it happens once in a while, but I’m not sure.
Did you have trouble paying attention or sitting still when you were a kid?

Yeah… I think so. My mom still brings it up sometimes. Like, teachers in elementary school would send notes saying I rushed through my work, lost homework, talked out of turn… and I guess I had trouble staying in my seat unless they reminded me.
Did you have any problems with impulsivity as a kid, like blurting out answers or interrupting others?

Yeah… I guess so. My mom still brings up notes from elementary school saying I talked out of turn a lot. I’d rush through work, lose homework, and had trouble staying in my seat unless someone reminded me.
Did you experience any of these symptoms, like restlessness or forgetfulness, before you were a teenager?
Yeah… before I was a teenager, definitely. My mom still mentions notes from elementary school—rushing through work, losing homework, talking out of turn, not staying seated unless I was reminded.
Have you experienced these symptoms, like restlessness and forgetfulness, pretty consistently throughout your adult life?
It’s been more noticeable lately… really since I moved into the supervisor role, about a year and a couple months ago. Before that, I guess it was there, but it didn’t feel like as much of a problem.
Have you noticed these symptoms, like restlessness and forgetfulness, in multiple areas of your life, such as at home, with friends, or in other activities outside of work?

Yeah… it’s not just work. Work is where it’s kind of on paper now—my manager put it in a formal review. But at home too, it causes arguments. People feel like they can’t really count on me to follow through.
Have you had these symptoms, like restlessness and forgetfulness, consistently since you were a child?

Yeah… I mean, from what I know, yes. I was like this as a kid too. My mom still brings up teacher notes from elementary school about me rushing through work, losing homework, talking out of turn, and needing reminders to stay seated.
